forces.title: High financing costs and economic uncertainty curb property investment
forces.description: Higher interest rates and construction costs, coupled with broader economic uncertainty, are making both households and businesses more hesitant to invest in new residential and non-residential properties across Europe. This dampens growth momentum for real estate development and slows down recovery in the building sector.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Rising input costs and difficult pass-through pressure project viability
forces.description: Higher energy prices are increasing production costs for energy-intensive building materials like concrete, cement, and bricks across Europe. However, it's becoming harder for real estate developers to pass these increased costs on to buyers and investors, who already face higher interest rates, leading to project unprofitability and postponements.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Supply chain disruptions from low water levels affecting material delivery
forces.description: Low water levels in inland waterways across Europe are creating upward cost pressure on building materials crucial for real estate development. Reduced barge cargo capacity increases transport costs and delays deliveries in the construction supply chain, leading to production constraints and potential project setbacks, impacting the timeliness and cost-efficiency of real estate projects.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: High interest rates and geopolitical uncertainty stall residential growth
forces.description: Higher interest rates are reducing housing affordability, particularly for new residential builds that require financing during construction. Geopolitical uncertainty, notably from the Middle East conflict, makes buyers more reluctant to commit to new homes with long completion periods, leading to a stabilization in building permit issuance and stalling residential real estate growth across Europe.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: New housing projects face commercial viability challenges and buyer preference for existing homes
forces.description: Despite severe housing shortages in many European cities, new residential projects struggle with commercial viability due to high construction costs. Real estate developers find it difficult to fully pass these costs to buyers, especially when existing homes remain cheaper. This dynamic leads buyers to prefer older properties and developers to postpone new construction, hindering market growth.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Rising energy/material costs and higher mortgage rates dampen housing affordability
forces.description: Increased energy prices are driving up building material costs (up 8% YoY in July 2026, with metals up 36%), pushing new home prices higher in Belgium. Simultaneously, elevated long-term interest rates and mortgage rates are reducing housing affordability, contributing to a ~10% decline in new mortgages and weakening order books for residential construction.
forces.source_title: Belgian building permit recovery continues, but challenges lie ahead

forces.title: Policy uncertainty on housing market taxes dampens demand
forces.description: The Flemish government's plan to increase registration duties on the sole family home introduces policy uncertainty in Belgium's housing market. This makes it harder for households to anticipate home purchase costs, potentially dampening demand further in a market already expected to lose momentum. Such policy shifts can significantly impact buyer sentiment and transaction volumes.
forces.source_title: Belgian building permit recovery continues, but challenges lie ahead

forces.title: Increasing value premium for energy-efficient homes due to rising energy costs
forces.description: Higher energy prices and stricter renovation standards are widening the price gap between energy-efficient and energy-intensive homes in Belgium. Energy efficiency is increasingly valued not only for reducing expenses but also as a hedge against future price shocks and regulatory risks, making it a critical determinant of property value and marketability for residential real estate.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Data centre buildout is a key growth driver for Norwegian economy
forces.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network contacts highlight data centre buildout as an important growth driver for Norway. This expanding activity directly increases demand for related real estate assets, contributing positively to output and investment growth in the region, particularly impacting domestic manufacturing of energy supply equipment and creating new investment opportunities in specialized real estate.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Terrestrial data centers face mounting constraints on land and power
forces.description: Traditional data centers are increasingly encountering significant limitations regarding land availability and power supply. These mounting constraints drive interest in alternative solutions, such as space-based data centers, highlighting a fundamental structural shift in the operational environment for data center real estate. Terrestrial facilities must address these core infrastructure challenges to remain competitive and expand.
forces.source_title: Space-Based Data Centers: More Than Hype, but Not a Revolution

forces.title: Space-based data centers pose long-term competition to terrestrial facilities
forces.description: While space-based data centers currently carry a 2.5x to 3x cost premium, this is expected to narrow to 1.5x within a decade, with satellites potentially capturing 10% to 15% of the global AI data center market by 2040. This represents a long-term risk for terrestrial data center real estate, as a portion of future demand may be diverted to orbital solutions, especially for latency-tolerant or sovereign AI workloads.
forces.source_title: Space-Based Data Centers: More Than Hype, but Not a Revolution

forces.title: AI and automation are transforming real estate services to improve efficiency
forces.description: Real estate services companies are increasingly adopting AI and automation to streamline highly manual processes, such as invoice matching and billing in finance functions. This structural shift allows organizations to focus on proprietary workflows, data, and customer relationships, differentiating their businesses by improving productivity and reducing operational friction through technological integration and partnerships.
forces.source_title: ...the AI dilemma: to build, buy, or partner.

forces.title: Significant capacity gap and robust investment in Irish healthcare real estate
forces.description: Ireland faces a substantial capacity gap in healthcare real estate, requiring 2,197 additional residential disability places and 1,039 nursing home beds annually. Despite existing nursing home bed stock decline, investment activity remains robust, driven by strong investor confidence and the strategic importance of disability accommodation, assisted living, and community-based care infrastructure, offering significant future opportunities.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Community pushback increasingly restricts data center development and expansion
forces.description: Growing community opposition is emerging as a significant force restricting new data center developments and expansions. This pushback can lead to project postponements and delays, impacting the ability to scale capacity efficiently. This risk, observed in other regions, is relevant for data center real estate across Europe, potentially complicating site acquisition and permitting for future projects.
forces.source_title: Powering AI: How real is the risk of overbuilding?

forces.title: Speculative interconnection requests distort data center power demand outlook
forces.description: The substantial backlog in data center load interconnection requests is partly driven by speculative and duplicative applications from developers and hyperscalers seeking to secure power rights. This 'queue gaming' distorts actual demand estimates, interferes with equipment ordering, strains EPC capacity, and complicates utility planning for data center real estate, necessitating measures like large-load tariffs.
forces.source_title: Powering AI: How real is the risk of overbuilding?

forces.title: Data center operators increasingly adopt on-site power for reliability and speed
forces.description: Due to grid constraints, uptime requirements, and speed-to-market needs, data center operators are increasingly deploying on-site power solutions like gas engines, turbines, fuel cells, and battery storage. This marks a structural shift towards permanent on-site generation, with a majority of industry leaders anticipating such deployments by 2030, transforming the power supply architecture for data center real estate.
forces.source_title: Powering AI: How real is the risk of overbuilding?

forces.title: Surging AI compute density drives adoption of higher-voltage DC power systems
forces.description: The increasing density of computing power in AI data center racks, with electricity needs climbing from under 50kW to 200-600kW per rack, necessitates a shift to higher-voltage DC (800 VDC) power systems. This structural change addresses inefficiencies of traditional low-voltage AC, reducing conversion losses, improving scalability, and optimizing space, creating new opportunities for electricity and component providers in data center real estate.
forces.source_title: The shift to 800-volt DC at data centers: Implications for providers

forces.title: Safety concerns and lack of standards hinder 800 VDC data center adoption
forces.description: The transition to 800 VDC systems in data centers faces significant barriers related to safety, as higher voltages introduce new shock, fault, and arc flash risks requiring new protocols. Additionally, the immaturity of industry standards, testing methods, equipment requirements, and installation guidelines compared to legacy AC systems slows broad adoption and necessitates collaborative development in data center real estate.
forces.source_title: The shift to 800-volt DC at data centers: Implications for providers

forces.title: Increased housing supply boosts sales but moderates price growth
forces.description: The Dutch housing market is experiencing a significant increase in homes listed for sale (up 20% YoY in June), including former rental properties, which is driving existing home sales to record highs. While this boosts transaction volumes and market mobility, the increased supply, combined with higher mortgage rates, is reducing upward pressure on house prices and moderating price growth expectations.
forces.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

forces.title: Hotel real estate investment shifts to enhancement over new-build expansion
forces.description: Capital investment in Irish hotel real estate is prioritizing refurbishment, repositioning, energy efficiency upgrades, and guest experience enhancements over speculative new-build expansion. This shift reflects a strategic focus on improving existing assets to protect relevance and pricing power in a market where mid-market and larger independent hotels need clearer differentiation amid market polarization.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Strong underlying demand and rising incomes support Dutch housing prices
forces.description: Despite increased supply and higher mortgage rates, the Dutch housing market remains tight, with homes selling quickly (within four weeks), indicating strong demand for owner-occupied properties. Rising household incomes (forecast 3% YoY wage growth) and increasing financial support for first-time buyers, including self-funding and municipal loans, continue to underpin and support residential house prices.
forces.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

forces.title: European real estate prices decline amid broader secular stagnation
forces.description: France and Germany, along with China, experienced a drop in 'paper wealth' due to declining real estate prices in 2025. This trend reflects Europe's broader economic gravitation towards 'secular stagnation,' characterized by sluggish demand depressing overall growth. Such conditions can directly impact the valuation and investment appeal of real estate assets across the region.
forces.source_title: The global balance sheet 2026: Imbalance and divergence

forces.title: Household real estate values recalibrate downward across eurozone economies
forces.description: Household real estate, the largest component of wealth, saw values relative to GDP continue to correct in 2025 across nearly all economies, including the eurozone. Values are now back to levels seen two decades ago in the eurozone, indicating a recalibration from pandemic peaks and reflecting a broader trend of declining real estate values impacting household wealth.
forces.source_title: The global balance sheet 2026: Imbalance and divergence

forces.title: Taxation and rent-cap policies constrain investment in Irish housing
forces.description: In Ireland, housing remains the weakest performing segment within construction, as specific taxation and rent-cap policies have constrained investment in residential development. Despite strong underlying demand, these regulatory measures deter new capital into housing projects, hindering supply growth and impacting the commercial viability for developers in certain areas of the housing real estate market.
forces.source_title: July 2026 Ireland Sector Snippets

viewpoints.title: Europe's residential and non-residential property investment remains subdued amidst headwinds
viewpoints.description: ING Research expects residential and non-residential property investment in Europe to remain weak. Higher interest rates, elevated construction costs, and persistent economic uncertainty are making households and businesses more cautious about investing in new properties. This results in subdued growth for the building sector, with a stronger residential recovery delayed despite a stabilization in housing permits, capping overall momentum.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: French residential real estate faces contraction due to weak confidence and permits
viewpoints.description: France's residential real estate sector is expected to contract by 2.5% in 2026. This negative outlook is driven by a significant fall in overall construction output, declining quarter-on-quarter, and weakening sector confidence. Housing permits in August remained below previous year levels, and sluggish GDP growth further exacerbates the challenges, leading to a projected contraction.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Spanish residential real estate set for recovery with rising permits and GDP growth
viewpoints.description: The Spanish residential real estate market is showing signs of recovery, with a forecasted growth of 3% in 2026. After a significant output decline between 2019 and 2022, the market rebounded. Building permits have risen sharply, easing from high levels. Robust GDP growth is expected to provide substantial support for housing construction this year and next, fostering continued recovery.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Dutch housing construction to gradually recover, driven by increased permits
viewpoints.description: The Netherlands' housing construction sector is anticipated to stabilize in 2026 following a weak first half, with modest growth expected in 2027. This recovery is predicated on the gradual translation of recent increases in building permits into housing starts and completions. However, the pace of recovery is expected to remain limited due to project delays from grid capacity issues and nitrogen restrictions.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: German housing market set for modest recovery after prolonged contraction
viewpoints.description: Germany’s housing market is expected to resume growth in 2026 after five consecutive years of contraction. Europe’s largest construction market saw a more than 10% decline from 2020 to 2025. A modest recovery is projected this year, with momentum gradually increasing into 2027, supported by housing demand and infrastructure investment, despite challenges in speeding up planning approvals.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Belgian building permits recover, but headwinds from costs and low volumes persist
viewpoints.description: Belgian building permit activity improved in H1 2026, with an 8% increase driven by new construction, especially residential (+14% YoY). However, overall permit volumes remain historically low. Higher energy prices pushing up building material costs (8% YoY) and rising financing costs due to geopolitical tensions are curbing momentum, alongside policy uncertainty from proposed increases in registration duties.
viewpoints.source_title: Belgian building permit recovery continues, but challenges lie ahead

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing market resilience masks weakening momentum due to financing conditions
viewpoints.description: Belgium’s housing market demonstrated unexpected resilience in Q2 2026, with modest price increases (+0.2% QoQ, +5.3% YoY) and a transaction recovery (+2.4% QoQ). However, underlying momentum is expected to weaken due to continued weak mortgage production (10% below last year) and persistently higher interest rates. Nominal median house prices are forecast to cool, with increases of 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Norwegian residential and commercial construction activity remains low, upturn delayed
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network reports persistently low construction activity in Norway, with few new residential and commercial projects. While residential construction shows some pickup in the South-West, the broader upturn is repeatedly delayed. Weak demand for housing and conventional commercial buildings, particularly in the Central region, continues to weigh on business conditions, despite an increase in state-level projects.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Dutch housing construction recovery remains limited despite surge in permits
viewpoints.description: The Dutch construction sector is expected to stabilize in 2026, with modest growth in 2027, primarily driven by housing construction. New-build home permits surged to a 10-year high in May 2026 (10,628), indicating future activity. However, construction starts lag permits significantly, and the recovery remains limited by delays from grid capacity and nitrogen restrictions, leading to only 71,000 new homes in 2026.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

viewpoints.title: Dutch housing market achieves record sales, but price growth moderates
viewpoints.description: The Dutch housing market is on track for a record year in sales, with an expected 245,000 existing homes changing hands in 2026, surpassing the 2017 peak. This is driven by increased supply (20% more listings YoY). However, higher mortgage rates (4.0% for 10-year fixed) and weaker consumer sentiment are moderating house price growth, forecast at 3% for 2026 and 1.5% for 2027.
viewpoints.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

viewpoints.title: Irish construction strengthens, commercial leads, but housing faces policy constraints
viewpoints.description: Irish construction activity continues to strengthen, showing broad-based recovery and rising employment, with commercial construction exhibiting the strongest growth. While housing remains the weakest segment, impacted by taxation and rent-cap policies, underlying demand is robust and expected to support long-term activity. The sector benefits from low debt and healthy cash positions, providing resilience against cost inflation and staff shortages.

demand_drivers.description: Demand for home care support services is projected to increase by 91% by 2040, driven by population ageing and a shift towards community-based care, supporting growth in assisted living and community healthcare infrastructure.
An additional 2,197 disability residential places are required nationally, highlighting significant investment opportunities in disability accommodation, supported living, and respite services.
Nursing home occupancy remained near full capacity at 94.9%, reinforcing strong demand fundamentals and ongoing consolidation opportunities for premium facilities.

Native 800 VDC systems could reduce power-related operating expenditures by about 8% to 10%, due to improved overall electrical efficiency and reduced I²R losses.
